questions.question: What is the angle (in degrees) between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 5:20 PM?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Hour hand** covers 3600 in 12 hours

Angular distance covered in **1 hour** = 360/12 = 300

Angular distance covered in **60 minutes** = 300

Angular distance covered in **1 minute** = 1/20

__Calculation:__

**Minute hand** covers 360 in 60 minutes

60 minutes = 3600

1 minute = 360/60 ⇒ 1 minute = 60

Here given time is **5:20 PM**

Minute = **20**

Angle covered by **minute hand** = 20 × 6 = 1200

Angle covered by **hour hand** = 5 × 30 + 20 × ½ = 150 + 10 = 160° 

Angle between **hour and minute hands** = 160 − 120 = 400

Hence, the angle between the hour and minute hands is 400

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** = |60H - 11M|over2

Here, **H = hours** and **M = minutes**.

Given **H = 5** and **M = 20**.

So, Angle = |60×5 - 11×20|over2

Angle = |300 − 220| / 2

Angle = 80 / 2 = 40°

Hence, the correct answer is **40°**

questions.question: Which physiographic division of India is geologically the oldest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peninsular Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is considered the oldest physiographic division of India, originating from the ancient supercontinent known as **Gondwanaland**.
 
• Geologically, it is a **stable shield** block composed of ancient **crystalline**, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks** that date back to the **Pre-Cambrian** era, making it far older than the **Himalayas**.
 
• The plateau was formed as a result of the breaking and drifting of the **Indian Plate** northward, eventually colliding with the **Eurasian Plate**.
 
• It covers a massive area of approximately **16 lakh square kilometers**, with an average elevation ranging between **600 to 900 meters** above sea level.
 
• The topography is characterized by **relict mountains** and **denuded hills** such as the **Aravallis**, which are among the oldest fold mountains in the world, further proving the geological antiquity of this region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**:

 
 
• These are classified as **Young Fold Mountains** that formed during the **Tertiary** period (approximately 40 to 50 million years ago) due to the **Alpine Orogeny**.
 
• They exhibit a high-relief topography with steep **V-shaped valleys** and **glaciers**, representing geological youth.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plains**:
 
 
• This region is an **aggradational plain** formed by the deposition of alluvium by the **Indus**, **Ganga**, and **Brahmaputra** rivers.
 
• It is the youngest physiographic division, belonging to the **Quaternary** period (Pleistocene and Holocene epochs).
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• Divided into the **Western Coastal Plain** and **Eastern Coastal Plain**, these were formed by **marine deposits** and **fluvial activity**.
 
• The **Western Coast** is an example of a **submerged coastline**, whereas the **Eastern Coast** is characterized by **emergent** features and large deltas.

questions.question: Which temple is an example of the Kalinga style of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagannath Temple, Puri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jagannath Temple** in **Puri**, Odisha, is a premier example of **Kalinga Architecture**, which is a regional sub-style of the **Nagara** (North Indian) temple architecture style.
 
• Constructed in the **12th century**, the temple was commissioned by **King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva**, the first monarch of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**.
 
• The temple complex follows a specific structural layout characteristic of the **Kalinga style**, comprising four main components: the **Vimana** (sanctum/Rekha Deula), the **Jagamohana** (assembly hall/Pidha Deula), the **Nata Mandira** (dance hall), and the **Bhoga Mandapa** (offering hall).
 
• It is famously known as the **White Pagoda** (to distinguish it from the **Konark Sun Temple** or Black Pagoda) and serves as one of the **Char Dham** pilgrimage sites for Hindus.
 
• The architecture is distinguished by its **curvilinear spire** (shikhara) and the absence of pillars in the main halls, a remarkable feat of **medieval engineering**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brihadeeswarar Temple**:

 
 
• Located in **Thanjavur**, it is a masterpiece of **Dravidian architecture** built by the **Chola King Raja Raja I**.
 
 
 
• **Meenakshi Temple**:
 
 
• Situated in **Madurai**, it represents the **Pandya** and **Nayaka** styles of **Dravidian architecture**, famous for its 14 towering **Gopurams**.
 
 
 
• **Shore Temple**:
 
 
• Located in **Mamallapuram**, it was built by the **Pallava Dynasty** under **Narasimhavarman II** and is one of the oldest structural stone temples in **South India**.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer can carry during a round?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Rule 4.1b** of the official **Rules of Golf**, a player is strictly prohibited from carrying more than **14 clubs** during a competitive round.
 
• This regulation was formally adopted in **1938** by the **United States Golf Association (USGA)** and later by **The R&A** to prevent an arms race of equipment that was making the game less about skill and more about having a specialized club for every possible shot.
 
• Before this rule, it was not uncommon for professional golfers to carry as many as **20 to 30 clubs**, which also placed an immense physical burden on **caddies**.
 
• A player may start a round with fewer than 14 clubs and add more during the play until the **14-club limit** is reached, provided the additions do not cause an **undue delay** to the game.
 
• The selection of the 14 clubs is entirely up to the golfer, typically including a mix of **woods**, **irons**, **wedges**, and a **putter**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Penalty Framework**:

 
 
• In **Stroke Play**, the penalty for exceeding the limit is **two strokes** for each hole where a breach occurred, with a maximum penalty of **four strokes** per round.
 
• In **Match Play**, the penalty results in a **deduction of holes**, where the match score is adjusted by one hole for each hole the breach occurred, up to a maximum of **two holes**.
 
• Once a player discovers they have more than 14 clubs, they must immediately perform an **out-of-play procedure** to declare which clubs will not be used for the remainder of the round.
 
 
 
• **Equipment Evolution**:
 
 
• Modern players often swap clubs based on **course conditions**; for instance, replacing a **long iron** with a **hybrid** or adding a **60-degree lob wedge** depending on the speed of the greens and the thickness of the rough.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of non-ferrous minerals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They lack iron content**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-ferrous minerals** are a specific category of **metallic minerals** that do not contain **iron** (scientifically known as **ferrum**) as a significant component.
 
• The primary distinguishing factor of these minerals is their chemical composition, which makes them highly resistant to **corrosion** and **rusting**, unlike their ferrous counterparts.
 
• These minerals are characterized by physical properties such as high **malleability**, low weight, and exceptional **thermal and electrical conductivity**.
 
• Common examples found in the **Earth's crust** include **copper**, **lead**, **zinc**, **tin**, and precious metals like **gold** and **silver**. **Bauxite**, the ore used for **aluminum** production, is one of the most widely used non-ferrous minerals globally.
 
• From a geological perspective, they are often found in **igneous** and **metamorphic rock** formations, often extracted through **veins** and **lodes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ferrous Minerals**:

 
 
• These are metallic minerals that contain **iron** as a base element.
 
• They account for about **three-fourths** of the total value of the production of metallic minerals.
 
• Major examples include **iron ore**, **manganese**, **chromite**, and **pyrite**.
 
• They are essential for the development of the **metallurgical industries** and the manufacturing of **steel**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Applications**:
 
 
• Because they **lack iron content**, non-ferrous minerals are vital in **aeronautical**, **electrical**, and **engineering** industries.
 
• **Copper** is indispensable in the **power industry** for cables and electronics, while **aluminum** is favored in **automobile** and **packaging** sectors due to its strength-to-weight ratio.

Sign Conventions

questions.question: A car covers a certain distance at a speed of 60 km/h. If the driver increases the speed by 25%, how much time will he save on a journey of 240 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed Ratio** (Original : New) = 100% : 125% = 4 : 5

Since **Distance** is constant, **Time Ratio** = 5 : 4

**Original Time** = 240 km ÷ 60 km/h = 4 hours = 240 min

5 units = 240 min → 1 unit (Time saved) = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 min

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Original speed = 60 km/h, Distance = 240 km, Speed increase = 25%.

**Formula:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/26d446b7206ee9d4fafe89be8b5afd64bd223210bf1e0c13b04e466c5afd6c27.png] 

⇒ **Original Time** = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 hours

⇒ **New Speed** = 60 + (25% of 60) = 60 + 15 = 75 km/h

⇒ **New Time** = 240 ÷ 75 = 3.2 hours

⇒ **Time Saved** = 4 − 3.2 = 0.8 hours

⇒ **Time Saved in minutes** = 0.8 × 60 = 48 min

**∴ The correct answer is 48 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Inverse Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed

For a journey with different speeds for equal distances, Average Speed = 2S₁S₂ ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert hours to minutes, multiply by 60.

Adding Unlike Fractions

Equivalent Fractions

Multiplying or dividing both the **numerator** and the **denominator** of a fraction by the same non-zero number does not change its value.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A fraction where the numerator is less than the denominator is a **Proper Fraction** (e.g., 11/12), whereas one where the numerator is greater or equal is **Improper**.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

BODMAS Rule

Decimal Point Shifting

When dividing decimals, you can shift the decimal point to the right in both the **dividend** and the **divisor** by the same number of places to work with whole numbers.

Decimal to Percentage

To convert a **decimal** like 0.17 to a **percentage**, multiply by 100 to get 17%.

questions.question: The side of a square is 21 cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?

For any **square** with side **a**, the length of the **diagonal** is always **a√2**.

Given **Side** = 21 cm.

**Diagonal** = 21 × √2 = 21√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 21√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Side** of the square (a) = 21 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **square**, a diagonal divides it into two **right-angled triangles**. Using the **Pythagoras Theorem**:

Diagonal (d) = √(Side² + Side²) = √(2a²) = a√2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eda2ce293d7ce6f805a86266386a2d6279abc21eafcbcbff2e1eb403ea3812b9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(21² + 21²)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(441 + 441)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(882)

⇒ **Diagonal** = √(441 × 2)

⇒ **Diagonal** = 21√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Square

The **Area** can be calculated as Side² or (Diagonal²) ÷ 2.

Perimeter of Square

The **Perimeter** (P) is the sum of all four sides: P = 4 × Side.

Ratio Property

For any square, the **ratio** of the **Side to the Diagonal** is always **1 : √2**.

Sum of first n natural numbers

General term of an AP

questions.question: Average of 50 results is 'N'. 4 is subtracted from each result. What will be the new average of these 50 results?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the **property of arithmetic mean**, if a constant value **k** is subtracted from every observation in a set, the **new average** also decreases by the same constant **k**.

Original Average = **N**

Value subtracted from each result = **4**

New Average = **N − 4**

**∴ The correct answer is N-4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total number of results = **50**, Old average = **N**, Subtraction constant = **4**.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9ecea326f7fbb1a43fb92fbf99b233c2f0763a8e956b57a00e9937ae54554af.png] 

⇒ Total sum of 50 results = 50 × N = 50N

⇒ Total reduction = Number of results × value subtracted from each = 50 × 4 = 200

⇒ New sum of 50 results = 50N − 200

⇒ New average = (50N − 200) ÷ 50

⇒ New average = 50(N − 4) ÷ 50

⇒ New average = N − 4

**∴ The correct answer is N-4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition of Constant

If a constant **k** is added to every observation, the new average becomes **Old Average + k**.

Multiplication by Constant

If every observation is multiplied by a constant **k**, the new average becomes **Old Average × k**.

Algebraic Sum of Deviations

The sum of the deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is **always zero**.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with counts n₁, n₂ and averages A₁, A₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question:
Average of some numbers is 'p'. 27 is the smallest number among these numbers. Which of the following statement will be always correct?

I. p = 30. II. 54 will be the largest number among these numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any set of **n numbers**, the average **p** must satisfy the condition: **Smallest ≤ p ≤ Largest**.

Given the **smallest number is 27**, we only know that **p ≥ 27** and **Largest ≥ 27**.

Since the other numbers in the set and the **total count n** are unknown, both **p** and the **largest number** can take any value ≥ 27.

Neither **p = 30** nor **Largest = 54** is a mandatory condition for all possible sets.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Smallest number in the set = 27. Average = **p**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e21d99a20698d5d979450882849bad09a0f1745d66c734a4f6accce64f1ea1c3.png] 

Let the numbers be x₁, x₂, x₃, ... , xₙ.

⇒ Smallest (x₁) = 27.

⇒ **Average (p)** = (x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ) ÷ n.

Checking Statement I: **p = 30**.

⇒ If set is {27, 28, 29}, **p** = (27 + 28 + 29) ÷ 3 = 28. (p ≠ 30).

⇒ If set is {27, 33}, **p** = (27 + 33) ÷ 2 = 30. (p = 30).

⇒ Statement I is **not always** correct.

Checking Statement II: **Largest = 54**.

⇒ If set is {27, 28}, Largest = 28. (Largest ≠ 54).

⇒ If set is {27, 54}, Largest = 54. (Largest = 54).

⇒ Statement II is **not always** correct.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Range of Average

The arithmetic mean or **average** always lies between the minimum and maximum values of a data set: **xₘᵢₙ ≤ p ≤ xₘₐₓ**.

Dependency on Number of Terms

To uniquely determine the **average (p)** or any specific term like the **largest number**, we must know the values of all other terms or specific properties of the distribution (like an AP).

Effect of Extremes

The **average** is highly sensitive to outliers. A very large maximum value will significantly pull the average **p** higher, regardless of the smallest value.

questions.question: What is the total number of positive factors of 180?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime factorize **180**: 180 = 2² × 3² × 5¹.

To find the **total number of factors**, add 1 to each exponent and multiply them.

Total factors = (2 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (1 + 1)

Total factors = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 factors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 180

**Formula Used:** If the prime factorization of a number N is ap × bq × cr, then the total number of positive factors = (p + 1)(q + 1)(r + 1).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2174eeac4cd9c2868713608672b4866477be2f6a7b428fae34d34f1c9c2ab958.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization: 180 = 2 × 90 = 2 × 2 × 45 = 2² × 3 × 15 = 2² × 3² × 5¹

⇒ Powers are p = 2, q = 2, r = 1

⇒ Total factors = (2 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (1 + 1)

⇒ Total factors = 3 × 3 × 2 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18 factors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Factors

The sum of all positive factors of N = apbqcr is given by [(ap⁺¹−1)/(a−1)] × [(bq⁺¹−1)/(b−1)] × [(cr⁺¹−1)/(c−1)].

Product of Factors

The product of all factors of a number N is equal to N⁽Total Number of Factors / ²⁾.

Perfect Square Factors

To find perfect square factors, only consider even exponents of the prime bases in the combinations.

questions.question: 50 percent of selling price of an article is equal to the 4/5 of the cost price of the article. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the parts: 50% SP = 4/5 CP ⇒ 1/2 SP = 8/10 CP

Ratio of SP : CP = 8/5

Profit = 8 − 5 = 3 units on a base of 5 units (CP)

Profit % = (3/5) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

50% of **Selling Price (SP)** = 4/5 of **Cost Price (CP)**

**Formula Used:**

**Profit** = Selling Price − Cost Price

**Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b9328d67fdc9208b2ca05edb63ab2878fe7b79e8a140fc1f7966ceb38a298183.png] 

⇒ (50/100) × SP = (4/5) × CP

⇒ (1/2) × SP = (4/5) × CP

⇒ SP / CP = (4/5) ÷ (1/2)

⇒ SP / CP = (4/5) × (2/1) = 8/5

⇒ Let **Cost Price** = 5 units and **Selling Price** = 8 units

⇒ **Profit** = 8 − 5 = 3 units

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (3 ÷ 5) × 100

questions.question: In a mixture alcohol and water are in the ratio of 4 : 9. Water is 25 litres more than alcohol. What is the quantity of water in the mixture?

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Future Perfect Tense**. The active structure is: **Will + Subject + have + V3 (Past Participle) + Object + ?**.
 
• To convert a **Future Perfect** interrogative sentence into **Passive Voice**, the following structure is applied: **Will + New Subject (Original Object) + have been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + New Object (Original Subject) + ?**.
 
• In this sentence, the subject is **they**, the verb is **finalised**, and the object is **the plans**. Following the rule, the object **the plans** becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The auxiliary verb **have been** must be used immediately after the new subject in the passive form to maintain the **Perfect Tense** aspect.
 
• The pronoun **they** is the subject in the active voice and changes to its objective case **them** when it becomes the agent in the passive voice.
 
• The phrase **by the end of this week** is an adverbial of time and remains at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning.

• **Assertive vs. Interrogative:** An interrogative active sentence must remain interrogative in its passive form. Options that change the sentence into a statement (Assertive) are grammatically incorrect for this transformation.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Agent:** The use of **by them** indicates the **doer** of the action. In passive voice, the emphasis shifts from the doer (**they**) to the receiver of the action (**the plans**).

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

options.text: The courier delivers a secret message yesterday.

The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.
The courier had delivered a secret message yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence 'A secret message was delivered by the courier yesterday' is in the **Passive Voice**. This is identified by the auxiliary verb **was** followed by the past participle **delivered** and the preposition **by**. Hence, the sentence structure follows the **Simple Past Passive** format: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject.

• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice, the **Object** of the passive sentence (the courier) must become the **Subject** of the active sentence. Hence, 'The courier' initiates the action.

• The original subject (a secret message) becomes the **direct object** in the active voice construction. Hence, it receives the action of the verb.

• The tense of the sentence is **Simple Past**. In the active voice, the verb must be in its **V2 (Simple Past)** form without any auxiliary verbs like 'was' or 'were'. The V2 form of 'deliver' is **delivered**. Hence, the verb phrase changes from 'was delivered' to 'delivered'.

• The **Adverb of Time** 'yesterday' remains unchanged and typically stays at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning and chronological context. Hence, the final active construction is 'The courier delivered a secret message yesterday.'

 **Additional Information__**

• Rules for **Voice Conversion** in different tenses:

• **Simple Present Tense**:

• Active: Subject + V1(s/es) + Object.

• Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 + by + Subject.

• **Past Continuous Tense**:

• Active: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

• Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject.

• **Past Perfect Tense**:

• Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

• Passive: Object + had + been + V3 + by + Subject.

• Analysis of incorrect options:

• **Delivers**: This represents the **Simple Present Tense**, which contradicts the past time marker 'yesterday'.

• **Was delivering**: This represents the **Past Continuous Tense**, indicating an ongoing action in the past rather than a completed one.

• The **syntactic structure** of the idiom involves two **nouns** joined by the **conjunction and**, creating a **legalistic redundancy** typical of **Early Modern English**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Linguistic Errors and Eggcorns**:

• **For all intensive purposes**: This is a classic example of an **eggcorn**, a phonetic **misinterpretation** of a phrase that sounds similar to the original but changes its meaning. **Intensive** is an **adjective** meaning **concentrated** or **thorough**, which does not logically fit the **adverbial** usage of the idiom.

• **For all intense and purposes**: This is a **malapropism** where the **adjective intense** (meaning extreme or acute) is substituted for the **noun intents**. It is **semantically nonsensical** in this context.

• **Historical Origins**:

Over centuries, the phrase was shortened and the **preposition for** became common in **American English**, while **to** remains frequent in **British English**.
